featured_reviews.name: Meer Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: my experience with jamboree was amazing, and they are a huge part of my jump from a 1450 to a 1510. starting off with the faculty, they were genuinely amazing and really good at explaining concepts and helping us solve the difficult questions, and we were also made aware of the “trap” questions that usually come on the sat, which is why i was able to improve so much. along with that, the jamboree dashboard had so many full length practice tests that i was 100% prepared before my actual sat, and they also had topic wise questions for both verbal and quants which was really helpful. additionally, i could also see a detailed analysis of each of my full length test, including how much time i take to solve each type of question, how much time i spend on a wrong answer vs a right answer, a score distribution chart, and all of this really helped me know where i stand. also, the questions in their full length tests were at the same difficulty level as the actual sat, which is a great thing because most bluebook tests are easier than the actual exam. even their support team was really great at addressing any technical difficulties i faced, and they constantly updated me with even the tiniest of things to ensure i dont miss out on any important updates. the learning material they gave me was also quite helpful, since that gave me the exact strategies to solve each type of question on the sat. and lastly, the doubt solving sessions they had for each full length tests really solved all of my queries i had in the questions i couldn’t answer. overall, i loved the experience at jamboree and i would 100% recommend it to anyone who wants a structured learning framework to prepare for their SATs.

Updated: This review is subjective, because I had joined the classes (1 month verbal crash course) around 11th November, about 1.5 months before my actual GMAT. and I had also taken only one test offered in the class. (out of 5-6)  Additionally, I had not attended the Quant classes , but had access to few online questions. The questions for Quant looked good, but please use your judgment and maybe do a trial beforehand.
This was the first result from a simple google search for GMAT classes in Mumbai. But overall the classes didn't help me much. There were many important topics which I think weren't covered in the class. Topics such as idioms for sentence correction were not discussed,  practice on "sentence meaning" in sentence correction, techniques in RC were not taught, and for CR techniques like the negation technique in Assumptions and the yes/no technique for evaluation were taught, but reasoning , cause-effect, and practice on hard questions was not sufficient. Practice was provided for major CR type questions though.Resources given were several homework sheets and to do in class sheets,  verbal question bank ( 200 questions, but more like grammar practice), and online tests. The online verbal practice material was easier compared to the actual GMAT and the GMAT prep software. The exercises for basic grammar were okay, but they are not enough for a hard sentence correction question.

Overall, it gave me a start for my studies, but covering major topics and finding tough questions was something I had to do on my own, I realized that after giving GMAT. I had joined the classes presuming that I can give gmat in 1.5 month after completing a 1 month crash course(20hrs) using this class; however, now I have realized that if the amount I had spent for these classes (~20k Rs), had been spent to do self study using books and online tests ( Powerscore CR bible, Manhattan SC guide, Aristotle SC grail, Manhattan RC guide) with a little more time given to self study, then my GMAT results could have been better.
